title: Lior and the Debt
premise: Lior Andrade, a burned-out interpreter who launders secrets for delegations that were never meant to succeed, is approached by Lena Villalobos, who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of doing. The debt she invokes is real, however: it belongs to the training network that manufactured interpreters like him, and it has marked him for collection. As Lior and Lena trace the network's ledger from Geneva safehouses to a decommissioned airfield, loyalty to his old handlers collides with the truth of what they made him. To survive past dawn, Lior must burn the network's archive and board the extraction flight as the man who chose his own name.
about_author: Cyrus Eastwick is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where peace was negotiated by people who preferred war. He writes thrillers about language, debt, and the people paid to stand between them.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In Geneva, Lior interprets for a doomed ceasefire delegation, then finds a note in his coat: a favor returned, with interest owed. He doesn't recognize the handwriting or the woman watching him across the café. Emotional beat: unease — his carefully anonymous life has been noticed.

chapters.title: Lena Villalobos
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She introduces herself and names a night in Sarajevo twelve years ago when Lior allegedly pulled her from a burning convoy. He remembers no such night. She shows him a photograph — his face, younger, in uniform he never wore. Beat: vertigo; identity begins to crack.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lena explains the debt: the network that trained 'attributed' interpreters keeps ledgers of favors as leverage, and Lior's account has been called in by someone inside it. Refusal means collection. Beat: dread mixed with a shameful thrill of being seen.

chapters.title: The Delegation Destined to Fail
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Back in session, Lior notices his translations are being edited mid-stream — someone upstream is steering the talks toward collapse. He realizes his own voice is a weapon he doesn't control. Beat: complicity and anger.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She takes Lior to a dead-drop archive and shows him pages of the network's ledger: names, favors, prices. His childhood mentor, Aldous Rehn, appears as a collector. Beat: betrayal — the father figure was the creditor.

chapters.title: What They Made
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, interleaved memory. Fragments surface: a school outside Trieste, drills in invented languages, erasure of biographies. He begins to suspect the Sarajevo rescue was implanted — or stolen from someone else. Beat: grief for a self he can't verify.

chapters.title: The Handler's Tea
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Rehn invites Lior to tea, warm and paternal, offering promotion if he delivers Lena. Lior accepts the tea and lies beautifully — the training working for him at last. Beat: cold empowerment laced with self-disgust.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Hiding in a Geneva safehouse, Lena admits her own ledger entry: she informed on the convoy in Sarajevo, and the rescue story was her penance construct. Lior learns the favor may be hers, not his. Beat: fury, then reluctant understanding.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Saved
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following the photo's provenance, they find Tomas, the actual rescuer — now a broken informant for the network. Tomas confirms the swap: Lior's biography was built on his deed. Beat: horror; belonging revealed as theft.

chapters.title: Collection Notice
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The network moves: an interpreter colleague of Lior's is found drowned, a ledger page left in his pocket. The message is clear — accounts close at dawn, at the airfield extraction. Beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Burning Question
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior proposes the unthinkable: not flee the flight, but use it — the network's archive travels with the collectors, and dawn is the only window when it leaves the vault. Beat: agency seized; fear transmuted into plan.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Liars
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In an abandoned tram depot, they rehearse the con: forged credentials, split-second interpretation switches, a dead man's voice on a phone line. Old mistrust thaws into partnership. Beat: fragile trust, almost tenderness.

chapters.title: The Archive Flight Manifest
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. They infiltrate the freight office and learn the archive flies under diplomatic seal — and that Rehn himself will escort it. Lior must sit across from his maker and interpret him into ruin. Beat: dread and dark anticipation.

chapters.title: Old Language
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A quiet chapter: over cheap wine, Lena and Lior trade the languages of their erased childhoods. She asks what name he'd choose if the ledger burned. He answers honestly for the first time. Beat: intimacy; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: The Turncoat's Price
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Tomas offers to testify against the network in exchange for protection — then disappears. Either the network took him, or he sold them out. The plan now runs on a clock with a hole in it. Beat: paranoia; every ally uncertain.

chapters.title: Night of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Pre-dawn infiltration of the airfield: Lena cuts power grids while Lior walks into the terminal wearing a dead man's credentials. Rehn greets him by his true childhood name. Beat: mask-off confrontation, electric with danger.

chapters.title: Interpreting the Collector
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the vault car, Lior must translate Rehn's orders to the guards — and subtly corrupts each one, turning security inward. Rehn senses the drift and speaks to him directly in their training cant. Beat: duel conducted entirely in subtext.

chapters.title: Firewall
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena reaches the archive bay and starts the burn as alarms rise. She is cornered by the collector who trained her, and chooses truth over the exit — broadcasting the ledger contents over the field frequency. Beat: sacrifice; loyalty finally aligned with truth.

chapters.title: Dawn Extraction
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Climax. With the archive burning and the plane prepping, Rehn offers Lior everything — restoration, a name, a history — if he boards. Lior refuses in his own words, untranslatable, and pulls the last ledger page from Rehn's coat. Beat: liberation through refusal.

chapters.title: The Flight That Left Without Them
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The plane departs carrying ash and compromised men; Rehn is taken off it by his own collectors, whose orders Lior rewrote. Lena and Lior walk the runway as the sun rises. Beat: exhausted triumph, grief for Tomas.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Weeks later, the leaked ledger dismantles the network publicly; the Sarajevo rescue is re-attributed to Tomas, posthumously honored. Lena testifies to her own guilt and is believed. Beat: reckoning; truth costs but pays.

chapters.title: A Name of His Own
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In a small Lisbon apartment, Lior signs a lease under a name he chose himself, and mails the final ledger page — blank — to no address at all. Lena knocks. Beat: quiet belonging earned, the debt closed.
